question: In the context of Bhakti-Sufi traditions of India, Manikkavachakar, a devotee of ______, composed beautiful devotional songs in Tamil.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manikkavachakar **or **Maanikka Vaasagar **was a** 9th-century Tamil poet **who wrote **Tiruvasakam**, a book of **Shiva’s hymns.**
 
• He was one of the major writers of Saivite Thirumurai.
 
• He was the principal adherent of the Nayanars traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Nayanars**
 **Alvars**
 
 

 Nayanars were devoted to Lord Shiva and his Avatars
 Alvars were devoted to Lord Vishnu and his Avatars
 
 

 Nayanars were active around the 6th-8th Century AD
 Although modern scholars consider the Alvars to be active between the 5th and 10th century AD, they are believed to have lived between 4200 BCE - 2700 BCE.
 
 

 The high priest of Raja Raja Chola I, Nambiyandar Nambi, compiled the hymn into a series of volumes called the thirumurai.
 The hymns of Alvars were made into a consolidated volume known as Divya Prabandha
 
 

 There were 63 Nayanars, who belonged to different caste backgrounds such as potters, “untouchable” workers, peasants, hunters, soldiers, Brahmanas, and chiefs.
 There were 12 Alvars, who came from equally divergent backgrounds, the best known being Periyalvar, his daughter Andal, Tondaradippodi Alvar and Nammalvar.
